title: Grounds for dissolution of marriage by Muslim woman

content.overview: A Muslim woman may obtain a decree on specified statutory grounds including disappearance, non-maintenance, imprisonment, failure of marital obligations, impotence, specified conditions, cruelty and other recognized Muslim-law grounds.

content.study: A Muslim woman may obtain a decree on specified statutory grounds including disappearance, non-maintenance, imprisonment, failure of marital obligations, impotence, specified conditions, cruelty and other recognized Muslim-law grounds.\n\nThe provision should be read with its provisos, connected sections and the applicable procedural framework. A complete analysis identifies the legal trigger, proving ingredients, evidence, exceptions, forum and precise relief.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: The provision is part of the statutory architecture governing family status, property, adoption, guardianship, succession or maintenance. Its object is implemented through the precise legal conditions stated in the Act. The cited Supreme Court authority provides the controlling doctrinal context: A bare assertion of talaq is not sufficient; the factum and legal validity of talaq must be established in accordance with law.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: Read s. 2 with every proviso, exception and cross-reference. Do not replace the enacted conditions with a general statement of family-law fairness. Connected provisions can change the result, including provisions on jurisdiction, proof, maintenance, succession, adoption effects or court permission.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body:
Identify the governing statute and confirm that s. 2 applies to the parties and transaction.
Identify every statutory ingredient, proviso and exception before drafting the relief.
Prove the legally relevant status, dates, relationships, documents and conduct with admissible evidence.
Check connected provisions that alter, qualify or supply the procedural route for the substantive right.
State the precise statutory consequence and distinguish it from neighboring family-law remedies.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: The party asserting the statutory consequence ordinarily bears the burden of proving the facts that activate the provision, subject to statutory presumptions and burden-shifting rules. Status records, marriage/adoption certificates, family registers, property records, income evidence, medical material and correspondence should be produced in admissible form. Electronic material must satisfy BSA 2023 s. 63 where applicable. Civil family disputes ordinarily proceed on a preponderance-of-probabilities standard; any connected criminal allegation must be analyzed separately.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Identify the competent Family Court/District Court or other statutory forum. Plead material dates, jurisdictional facts, prior proceedings, statutory prerequisites and the exact relief. Limitation is provision-specific: many matrimonial-status and maintenance claims have no single universal period, while adoption/property/instrument challenges can attract particular Limitation Act Schedule articles. Never insert a generic limitation period without checking the precise cause of action.

examples.body: The claimant satisfies every material condition of s. 2. The pleadings identify the statutory trigger, the evidence proves the required status and dates, and no applicable exception defeats the claim.

examples.body: A material statutory condition for s. 2 is absent or an exception applies. The court should reject the assumed consequence unless the missing ingredient is proved or the exception is displaced by the statute.

misconceptions.trap: Treating s. 2 as automatic once a family relationship is shown.
misconceptions.correction: The relationship is only the starting point; the statutory ingredients, exceptions and evidence must still be established.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a parallel maintenance, custody, succession or matrimonial remedy automatically replaces s. 2.
misconceptions.correction: Substantive entitlement and procedural remedy must be analyzed separately. A parallel route may coexist, but it does not rewrite the governing provision.
